thread:
oncall-alex: :rotating_light: Paging — seeing a cluster of events in us-west-2. Multiple nodes reported ECC corrected spikes, then immediate Xid driver resets and several kubelets restarted containers. Observed 5xx spike on realtime/api and a few pods OOM-killed after restart. I'm taking initial triage.
infra-bot: Automated alert: 1881234567 - region=us-west-2 cluster=redwood-prod-gpu nodes=[i-0a1b2c3d4e, i-0f1e2d3c4b] events=[NVRM: Xid (79) 13, ECC corrected, GPU reset, kernel: oom_kill_process]
oncall-alex: Quick status: route /realtime latency up ~120ms, 5xx rate ~4.2% over last 5m. Infra shows node GPU ECC counts rising for ~10m, then a driver reset cascade. A few pods came back and hit memory pressure, got OOMKilled.
eng-runtime-jordan: Noted. Logs show repeated: ``NVRM: Xid (79) 13 at ..`` followed by ``nvidia: GPU fault, resetting``. After reset some containers failed liveness and restarted, causing memory spike. Could be thermal/firmware or bad ECC memory.
sre-maya: Actions to take now:
- cordon affected nodes: ``kubectl cordon <node>``
- drain non-critical pods with ``kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``
- scale down batch jobs in us-west-2 to free GPUs
- enable fallback routing to other regions by flipping traffic weight

oncall-alex: Doing cordon/drain now. Running:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-2.compute.internal
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
```

support-lina: Customer impact: we've got ~12 support tickets correlated to 1881234567 (realtime errors). Priority customers A/B are seeing degraded responses; informing account owners. ETA messaging: "We are investigating. Some requests may return 5xx intermittently."

eng-runtime-jordan: Suggest immediate mitigations:
- switch realtime route to model-variant-lowmem (less GPU memory pressure)
- enable aggressive prefix caching for hot flows
- disable async batching for affected pods temporarily

oncall-alex: Applied route change to fallback variant and increased cache TTLs. Monitoring for regression.

infra-bot: Runbook step: collect diagnostics from node before reboot. Commands: ``dmesg | tail -n 200``, ``journalctl -u kubelet -n 200``, ``nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CECC``. Save to /tmp/incident-1881234567/

eng-runtime-jordan: Paste of dmesg (excerpt):
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (79) 13 detected on GPU 0: PBDMA cache timeouts
[ 1234.568001] NVRM: GPU ecc error: 1 corrected, 0 uncorrected
[ 1234.568200] Kernel panic - not syncing: Out of memory: Killed process 4521 (runtime) total-vm:2456780kB
```

sre-maya: We should open a high-priority case with cloud provider and request hardware diag. Also schedule node replacement (terminate to get fresh host). For now we'll cordon and reboot if soft reset doesn't stabilize.

oncall-alex: Replaced two nodes (terminated EC2), autoscaling spun up new instances. Observed regression to baseline after node replacement. 5xx rate falling to ~0.6%.

customer-alert-bot: Incident 1881234567: Impacted customers receive notification: "Intermittent errors for realtime endpoint in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress; we have routed traffic and replaced affected hosts."

support-lina: Noting customers who need follow-up: acct-omega, acct-sigma. Preparing post-incident message with timeline.

sre-maya: Handing off to night shift. Current state: nodes cordoned, two bad hosts replaced, traffic routed to fallback variant, error rates largely recovered but watching for reoccurrence. Next steps for night: 1) Provider hardware ticket, 2) run burn-in stress on replacement hosts, 3) collect and attach ECC counts + nvidia logs to ticket.

oncall-alex: Handoff notes attached to runbook path /incidents/1881234567/handoff.md and logs in S3 s3://redwood-incident-logs/1881234567/

sre-maya: Acknowledge. Taking over. If anything spikes ping @sre-maya, escalation if >2% 5xx for >10m.

oncall-alex: Thanks — leaving detailed commands and notes in thread. :white_check_mark:

sre-maya: Handoff complete. Closing active paging but keeping incident in monitoring for 12h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
